q: For palmar hyperhidrosis, which level of the sympathetic chain is usually divided?
why: T2–3 for palmar hyperhidrosis, T2–4 for axillary, and T2–5 for angina or other indications.

q: After thoracic sympathectomy a patient has ptosis and miosis on one side. What has happened?
o: Horner’s syndrome from injury at the stellate (T1) level
why: Horner’s syndrome is a recognised delayed complication when the dissection reaches the stellate ganglion.

q: During ETS with intrathoracic CO2 insufflation, BP falls suddenly and airway pressures rise. What is the most likely cause?
why: Insufflation can cause tension pneumothorax, surgical emphysema and reduced venous return with hypotension. Release the gas and treat.

q: Which airway technique is often the first choice for bilateral ETS?
o: Single-lumen tube with intrathoracic CO2 insufflation
why: A single-lumen tube with CO2 insufflation is often first choice; a DLT gives the best access but adds atelectasis, shunt and hypoxaemia risk when both sides are operated on.

q: Which is an ABSOLUTE indication for one-lung ventilation?
o: Isolating a lung to prevent contamination from massive haemorrhage
why: Absolute indications are lung isolation to prevent contamination (haemorrhage, empyema), controlling ventilation distribution (bronchopleural fistula, bullae) and unilateral lung lavage.

q: What size double-lumen tube is usually chosen for an adult male?
why: By height: male under 170 cm 39 Fr, over 170 cm 41 Fr; female under 160 cm 35 Fr, over 160 cm 37 Fr. Position is confirmed clinically and then by bronchoscopy.

q: What is a disadvantage of a bronchial blocker compared with a DLT?
o: No suction or CPAP to the isolated lung and more likely to migrate
It cannot be used in difficult airways
It is larger and more rigid
It cannot isolate the left lung
why: Blockers go through an existing ETT (no exchange) but migrate more easily and do not allow suction or CPAP to the isolated lung.

q: Which nerve injury is associated with the lateral position?
why: The lateral position risks radial, common peroneal, brachial plexus and saphenous injuries, as well as eye and ear injury.

q: After turning lateral, peak airway pressure on one-lung ventilation rises from 25 to 40 cmH2O. What is the most likely cause?
why: Tube malposition is common after turning. Check with the bronchoscope. The narrow DLT lumen can also be obstructed.

q: What is the commonest long-term complaint after sympathectomy for hyperhidrosis?
why: Compensatory sweating elsewhere on the body is a common delayed complication and should be part of consent.
